Consult Summary:
- Telehealth consult for new-onset, severe persistent headache for 3 days with photophobia and visual disturbance; partial, temporary relief with ibuprofen.
- Clinician impression: probable migraine (possible aura). In-person neurological and fundoscopic examination and BP check arranged; stronger NSAID prescribed; ED precautions provided.

Problem List:

Issue 1:
- Acute severe headache, 3 days
  - Onset: Sudden on awakening, 3 days ago; constant since onset.
  - Character/location: Diffuse; worse over right supraorbital area; severity ~8/10, decreases to ~5/10 with ibuprofen.
  - Associated symptoms: Photophobia; intermittent “shooting light”/visual disturbance; mild nausea without vomiting; not waking from sleep; present on waking; brief stabbing pain when standing quickly.
  - Pertinent negatives: No focal neurologic symptoms (no weakness, numbness, tingling); no fever (not checked but does not feel feverish); no sinus symptoms or URI; no cough/hemoptysis; no epistaxis; no change in smell/taste.
  - Prior headaches: Infrequent, mild pressure between eyes; resolved with ibuprofen; no prior visual symptoms or nausea/vomiting.
  - Examination: None performed yet (teleconsult); plan for neurological exam and fundoscopy.
  - Clinical impression: Probable migraine; possible aura given visual phenomena. Duration and severity warrant in-person assessment to exclude secondary causes.
  - Impact: Interfering with work from home; required time off.

Issue 2:
- Contraceptive management in context of possible migraine with aura
  - Medication: On oral contraceptive pill for ~1 year; no noted side effects; no prior increase in headache frequency until current episode.
  - BP: Reported normal at pharmacy 1 year ago; not recently rechecked.
  - Family history: Mother with severe migraines with vomiting.
  - Plan: Recheck BP; if migraine with aura confirmed, combined OCP may be contraindicated—consider alternative contraception.

Issue 3:
- Work/functional impact
  - Works from home; reduced productivity and missed work due to headache.

Medications:
- Ibuprofen (over-the-counter), dose/route/frequency not documented; partial relief.
- Oral contraceptive pill (specific type/dose/route/frequency not documented).
- New prescription: Stronger NSAID “similar to ibuprofen” (name/dose/route/frequency not documented); advised may take with paracetamol; take with food.
- Paracetamol advised concurrently with prescribed NSAID (dose/route/frequency not documented).

Allergies:
- No known drug allergies reported.

Past Medical History:
- Remote history of unspecified pain in youth; no cause found; resolved. No other conditions reported.

Social History:
- Lives alone.
- Non-smoker.
- Alcohol: Drinks weekly; quantity unclear.
- No recreational drug use reported.
- No recent travel abroad.

Preventative History:
- Blood pressure reported normal at pharmacy 1 year ago (associated with OCP dispensing).
- No other preventive screenings or vaccinations discussed.

Physical Examination:
- Not performed (teleconsult). No vitals obtained.

Plan:
- Arrange in-person appointment for:
  - Full neurological examination.
  - Fundoscopic (retinal) examination.
  - Blood pressure measurement.
- Start prescribed stronger NSAID; may use paracetamol concurrently; take with food.
- Safety net: If headache worsens, changes in character, becomes unbearable, or new symptoms develop (e.g., persistent vomiting, neurologic deficits), attend emergency department; may call clinic for further advice.
- Contraception review: If migraine with aura is confirmed, discuss discontinuation of current combined OCP and alternatives.
- If symptoms resolve before appointment, consider canceling per clinician advice.
- Follow-up: Clinic visit as scheduled; reassess headache pattern, response to treatment, and contraception suitability.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements: Exact OCP name and regimen; doses/frequency for ibuprofen, paracetamol, and new NSAID; vitals; neurological and fundoscopic exam findings; detailed alcohol intake; pregnancy status not discussed.
- Internal conflicts: None noted; minor ambiguity regarding exact quantity of alcohol and work days off.
- Transcript quality: Some audio gaps/inaudible sections (patient identifiers, OCP name); otherwise understandable.
